transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump has changed his mind and will hold rallies in Kansas and Iowa this weekend.
NPR's Franco Ordonez reports Trump says Republican officials asked him to reconsider his decision
to cancel.
The president had said earlier that he was canceling those visits because Republicans
were in good shape in those states, but now he's taking a different tack.
"We got a call from Iowa and from the people and from my friends that are very, very good.
And we have a couple of races that are very important.
And they said if you could go, it would be better than a teller rally.
And I tried to talk about that, I said what about a teller rally?
But they asked me, so I'm going to do two on Sunday."
The president says he's not going on Saturday because of college football, but would leave
early Sunday morning for Iowa and then head to Kansas.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News, the White House.
All the votes have now been counted in Israel's election, as NPR's Ruth Sherlock reports Prime
Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has lost its majority in parliament.
Both Netanyahu's bloc and the main opposition failed to secure the 61 seats in the Israeli
parliament needed to form a government.
What follows are complex negotiations and horse trading as each side tries to build the coalition
it needs to reach a majority.
A key question is whether the center-right opposition will partner with Arab-led parties
who won a record 19 seats in this election.
Since the October 7th Hamas attacks on Israel three years ago, Arab leaders have been demonized
in Israel.
But partnering with them is one route to unseat Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime
minister.
Ruth Sherlock, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
A pair of new blood tests can help doctors determine whether a patient has Alzheimer's
disease.
John Hamilton reports that the tests offer an alternative to costly brain scans.
The blood tests measure a protein called PTOW 217.
It's closely associated with the presence of amyloid plaques in the brain, a hallmark
of Alzheimer's.
Dr. David Holtzman of Washington University School of Medicine helped develop the approach.
That particular test is extremely accurate at determining whether you have amyloid in
the brain or not.
Nearly as good as a costly PET scan.
Holtzman says the new blood tests are meant for older people who are already experiencing
problems with memory and thinking, not people who are just curious about their brain health.
They were approved by the Food and Drug Administration this summer.
For NPR News, I'm John Hamilton.
Krista Pike says she isn't in constant pain since surviving a botched lethal injection
in Tennessee last month.
Pike says she went into the execution chamber prepared to die in peace but woke up confused
in a hospital bed.
Pike was sentenced to death for torturing and killing a classmate when she was 18.
Pike says she had not contemplated life beyond her execution date and is thankful for the
medical workers who saved her.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Doc workers are staging strikes as part of an international campaign against arms shipments
and to demand better working conditions.
Unions in countries like France, Italy, Greece, Spain, Turkey, and Morocco are calling for
an end to the militarization of ports.
They say more than 100 ports are participating, which could affect operations in Europe, North
Africa, and North America.
Parts of the Southwest are still recovering from flooding after thunderstorms dropped
intense rainfall last week.
Chris Clements of member station KNAU reports rural communities and tribal nations are bracing
for another storm.
Arizona election officials say they're concerned about the ability of Navajo Nation residents
to reach polling places after previous floods wiped out roads.
Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs says she's considering all options to help counties dealing with
the disaster, which prompted evacuations and caused tornadoes to touch down.
We've been in constant communication with emergency managers at the county level and
at the tribal level, providing support where we can.
This weekend's storm could cause more flooding on the Navajo and Hopi reservations starting
Saturday night into early Monday morning.
For NPR News, I'm Chris Clements in Flagstaff.
Five Spanish missionaries are being elevated one step away from St. Hood nearly 430 years
after they were killed in present-day Georgia.
The Catholic Diocese of Savannah will hold a beatification ceremony for the five Franciscan
friars.
They were killed in 1597 by indigenous people they had traveled to the New World to baptize
in what historical records say was a dispute over polygamy.
This is NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: Trump reverses course and will rally in Iowa and Kansas on Sunday after GOP requests
Netanyahu's bloc loses parliamentary majority in Israel's election; coalition talks begin
New FDA-approved blood tests can help doctors determine whether patients have Alzheimer's disease
Krista Pike says she is no longer in constant pain after botched Tennessee lethal injection
Dockworkers in six countries strike against arms shipments and for better working conditions
Arizona officials and Governor Katie Hobbs respond to flood damage on Navajo and Hopi reservations
Five Spanish Franciscan missionaries killed in 1597 in Georgia set for beatification in Savannah
